entries.title: Mamata Banerjee alleges fake voters via duplicate voter ID numbers
entries.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee alleged that voters from states such as Haryana and Gujarat shared voter ID (EPIC) numbers with West Bengal voters, and accused the BJP of adding fake voters with the Commission's backing.
entries.attributed_to: Mamata Banerjee, Chief Minister of West Bengal (TMC)

sources.title: No fake voters, duplicate IDs stem from manual system: EC refutes Didi's charge

entries.notes: Exact day of the allegation not verified in the source opened; the Commission replied on 2 March 2025.

entries.title: Rahul Gandhi records dissent as panel picks Gyanesh Kumar for CEC
entries.summary: At the selection committee meeting with the Prime Minister and Home Minister, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi recorded a dissent note. He argued the panel, which no longer includes the Chief Justice of India, departed from the Supreme Court's March 2023 ruling and that the choice should wait for the Supreme Court hearing due on 19 February. The Law Ministry notified Kumar's appointment the same night.
entries.attributed_to: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, Lok Sabha

sources.title: CEC Selection: Rahul Gandhi Calls PM, HM's 'Midnight Decision' Choosing Gyanesh Kumar As 'Disrespectful, Discourteous' In Dissent Note
'Disrespectful, discourteous to appoint new CEC now': Rahul Gandhi says in dissent note

entries.notes: No government response to the dissent note itself was found in the sources opened; the appointment was notified regardless. The appointments area should hold the notification.

verification.note: ETV Bharat's report matches the entry point for point: the Monday meeting with PM/HM, the dissent citing the March 2023 ruling and the CJI's exclusion, the 19 Feb Supreme Court hearing, and the same-night Law Ministry notification. The Week's source URL returned Access Denied; not essential since ETV Bharat independently confirms all details.

entries.title: Commission says duplicate EPIC numbers do not mean fake voters
entries.summary: The Commission said identical EPIC numbers arose from the old manual, decentralised numbering before the database was digitised, that other details such as constituency and polling booth differ, and that affected voters would get unique numbers.
entries.attributed_to: Election Commission of India

sources.title: No fake voters, duplicate IDs stem from manual system: EC refutes Didi's charge

entries.title: Commission promises to fix duplicate EPIC numbers within three months
entries.summary: Facing allegations of a cover-up, the Commission said it would give a unique national EPIC number to electors holding duplicate numbers within three months, and that a voter can vote only at the polling station where they are enrolled.
entries.attributed_to: Election Commission of India

sources.title: Will resolve duplicate voter IDs issue in 3 months: Election Commission

entries.notes: Whether the three-month target was met is not covered here.

entries.title: Commission calls Maharashtra rigging charge absurd, points to December 2024 reply
entries.summary: The Commission said the charge was unsubstantiated, that trying to defame it after an unfavourable verdict was absurd, and that it had answered the same points in its reply to the Congress of 24 December 2024, published on its website. Commission functionaries also told reporters that the Congress had cancelled a meeting the Commission offered for 15 May.
entries.attributed_to: Election Commission of India (statement and unnamed functionaries)

sources.title: ECI Slams Rahul Gandhi's Allegations on Maharashtra Polls as Baseless
Completely absurd: Election Commission debunks Rahul Gandhi's match fixing claim

entries.notes: Media reports say the Commission also wrote to Rahul Gandhi on 12 June 2025; that letter was not opened. The 24 December 2024 reply was not opened.

entries.title: Rahul Gandhi asks Commission for machine-readable rolls and CCTV footage
entries.summary: Replying to the Commission's source-based rebuttal, Rahul Gandhi said a constitutional body should not answer through unsigned notes, and asked it to publish consolidated machine-readable voter rolls and release post-5 pm CCTV footage from Maharashtra polling booths.
entries.attributed_to: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, Lok Sabha

sources.title: Completely absurd: Election Commission debunks Rahul Gandhi's match fixing claim

entries.notes: The CEC answered the CCTV and machine-readable roll points on 17 Aug 2025; see that entry.

entries.title: Rahul Gandhi's op-ed alleges 'match-fixing' in 2024 Maharashtra election
entries.summary: In an Indian Express op-ed shared on X, Rahul Gandhi set out five steps he said were used to rig the November 2024 Maharashtra election, from the Election Commission appointment panel to adding voters and inflating turnout, and said Bihar would be next. BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari called the charge an attack on democratic institutions.
entries.attributed_to: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, Lok Sabha

figures.label: voters added between 2024 Lok Sabha and 2024 Maharashtra Assembly polls, per Rahul Gandhi

sources.title: How to steal an election: Maharashtra elections were rigged, so will Bihar be, alleges Rahul Gandhi

entries.notes: The 41 lakh figure is the claimant's. The Commission's own figures for the period (48.8 lakh added, 8 lakh deleted) are reported in the Indian Express piece of 23 Sep 2026 on Uddhav Thackeray; see that entry.

entries.title: Karnataka CEO says voter Rahul cited voted once; Maharashtra, Haryana seek declarations
entries.summary: The Karnataka CEO's notice said that on inquiry, Shakun Rani, whom Rahul Gandhi said had voted twice, stated she voted once, and asked for the documents behind the claim. The Maharashtra and Haryana CEOs separately asked him to submit signed declarations and documents within 10 days.
entries.attributed_to: Chief Electoral Officers of Karnataka, Maharashtra and Haryana

sources.title: EC Issues Notice To Congress Leader Rahul Gandhi For Allegations Of Voter Fraud In 2024 Lok Sabha Polls

entries.notes: Reported on 11 Aug 2025 early morning, so the notices date from on or before 10 Aug; exact day not verified.

entries.title: Rahul Gandhi says Congress has 'atom bomb' proof of vote theft
entries.summary: Speaking at Parliament House, Rahul Gandhi said a six-month Congress investigation had found proof that the Commission was engaged in 'vote chori' for the BJP, and warned officials involved that they would not be spared.
entries.attributed_to: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, Lok Sabha

sources.title: What we have found is an atom bomb; there's 100% proof EC doing vote chori for BJP: Rahul Gandhi

entries.notes: The evidence was presented on 7 Aug 2025; see that entry and the Commission's responses.

entries.title: Commission shows Tejashwi Yadav's name on draft roll; questions second card
entries.summary: The Commission shared the draft roll showing Yadav at serial number 416 in Digha constituency. On 3 August the Digha Electoral Registration Officer said the EPIC card Yadav displayed had not been issued officially and asked him to hand it over for investigation.
entries.attributed_to: Election Commission of India; Patna District Election Officer; ERO, Digha

sources.title: Election Commission debunks Tejashwi Yadav's name not in draft electoral roll claim
EC asks Tejashwi Yadav to furnish details of Voter ID shown at press meet; says card not issued by it

entries.title: Tejashwi Yadav says his name is missing from Bihar draft roll
entries.summary: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav searched his EPIC number on the Commission's site at a press conference, said it returned 'not found', and accused the Commission of working for the BJP after the Bihar SIR draft roll was published on 1 August.
entries.attributed_to: Tejashwi Yadav, Leader of Opposition, Bihar Assembly (RJD)

sources.title: Election Commission debunks Tejashwi Yadav's name not in draft electoral roll claim

entries.title: Karnataka and Maharashtra CEOs ask Rahul Gandhi to sign declaration under oath
entries.summary: Hours after the press conference, the Chief Electoral Officers of Karnataka and Maharashtra wrote to Rahul Gandhi asking him to sign a declaration under Rule 20(3)(b) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and to name the specific electors so proceedings could begin.
entries.attributed_to: Chief Electoral Officers of Karnataka and Maharashtra

sources.title: 'Sign under oath': Karnataka and Maharashtra CEOs challenge Rahul Gandhi's 'poll rigging' allegations
Rahul vs EC on 'vote chori': Karnataka poll body chief asks for names of electors; wants 'declaration under oath'

entries.notes: Commentators quoted by ADR/The Quint argued Rule 20(3)(b) applies to claims and objections during roll revision, not to general public allegations; that argument was not verified here.

entries.title: Rahul Gandhi alleges 1,00,250 fake voters in Mahadevapura segment
entries.summary: At a press conference, Rahul Gandhi presented Congress's analysis of the Mahadevapura Assembly segment of Bangalore Central, which the BJP won by 32,707 votes in 2024. He alleged 1,00,250 bad entries: duplicate voters, fake or invalid addresses, bulk voters at single addresses, invalid photos and misuse of Form 6. Asked to sign a declaration, he said his public statement could be taken as an oath.
entries.attributed_to: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, Lok Sabha

figures.label: alleged fake or invalid voters, Mahadevapura (Congress analysis)
alleged bulk voters at single addresses

sources.title: EC colluding with BJP to steal elections: Rahul Gandhi alleges 'massive' vote chori, cites Bangalore Central seat as example
'Sign under oath': Karnataka and Maharashtra CEOs challenge Rahul Gandhi's 'poll rigging' allegations

entries.notes: All breakdown figures are the Congress's claims. No signed declaration or affidavit was filed, per the Commission; see responses.

entries.title: Commission tells Rahul Gandhi to sign declaration or apologise
entries.summary: In a social media post, the Commission said Rahul Gandhi should either sign the declaration or apologise to the nation, and that not signing would mean he did not believe his own analysis. It said the Congress filed hardly any appeals during the 2024 roll preparation and that it had answered his December 2024 Maharashtra points.
entries.attributed_to: Election Commission of India

sources.title: ECI Rejects Rahul Gandhi's Vote Theft Allegations, Demands Apology or Signed Declaration

entries.notes: The Commission's post on X itself was not opened; this is the public broadcaster's report of it.

entries.title: At Bengaluru rally, Rahul Gandhi repeats Mahadevapura charge
entries.summary: At a 'Vote Adhikar' rally in Bengaluru, Rahul Gandhi repeated the 1,00,250 figure, asked the Commission to hand over electronic voter lists and ten years of videography, and asked the Karnataka government to investigate.
entries.attributed_to: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, Lok Sabha

sources.title: LoP LS Rahul Gandhi Again Accuses Election Commission Of Vote Theft In Bengaluru

entries.notes: No direct response to this statement was found in the sources opened.

entries.title: Opposition MPs detained while marching to Election Commission
entries.summary: About 300 INDIA bloc MPs led by Rahul Gandhi marched from Parliament towards Nirvachan Sadan against the Bihar SIR and alleged vote theft, and were detained and later released by Delhi Police. Police said the Commission had permitted 30 MPs to meet the Commission; the opposition wanted all MPs heard. Rahul Gandhi said of the affidavit demand that it was the Commission's data, not his to sign.

sources.title: Protest over SIR: INDIA bloc MPs march towards Election Commission's office from Parliament, Delhi Police stop procession enroute
'Vote Chori' row: Rahul Gandhi responds to Election Commission notice

entries.title: BJP's Anurag Thakur alleges doubtful voters in opposition leaders' seats
entries.summary: At the BJP headquarters, BJP MP Anurag Thakur alleged irregular entries in seats won by opposition leaders, including Rae Bareli, Wayanad, Diamond Harbour and Kannauj, citing for example 47 voter IDs at one Rae Bareli house number, and asked Rahul Gandhi to explain. The Congress said this confirmed that flawed rolls exist.
entries.attributed_to: Anurag Thakur, BJP MP

sources.title: Anurag Thakur slams Rahul Gandhi over 'vote theft' allegations, cites cases from Rae Bareli, Wayanad, Bengal

entries.notes: Whether the Commission asked Thakur for a signed declaration, as it did Rahul Gandhi, was not established in the sources opened.

entries.title: CEC Gyanesh Kumar: file affidavit in seven days or apologise
entries.summary: At the National Media Centre, CEC Gyanesh Kumar said Rahul Gandhi must give a signed affidavit within seven days or apologise, failing which the allegations would be treated as baseless. He called the bias charge an insult to the Constitution, said sharing CCTV footage of voters would breach their privacy, said Maharashtra's CEO had not received a single named voter with proof, and explained last-hour turnout as an average of about 10% an hour.
entries.attributed_to: Gyanesh Kumar, Chief Election Commissioner

sources.title: Give affidavit or apologise, no third option: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Rahul Gandhi's 'vote theft' allegations
sources.quote: Teesra koi vikalp nahi (There is no third option.)

sources.title: INDIA bloc considering motion to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar

entries.notes: No transcript on eci.gov.in or PIB was located. The Commission's later position was that no affidavit was filed. Whether Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi attended was not verified.

entries.title: INDIA bloc floor leaders discuss motion to remove the CEC
entries.summary: The day after the CEC's press conference, a meeting of opposition floor leaders in Parliament discussed moving a motion to remove Gyanesh Kumar, according to sources quoted by The Hindu.

sources.title: INDIA bloc considering motion to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar

entries.notes: No notice was filed in 2025; the first notices were filed on 12 March 2026.

verification.note: Free portion of The Hindu's report confirms the Aug 18, 2025 floor-leaders' meeting discussed a removal motion; the article's own photo caption places the CEC's press conference on 17 Aug 2025, supporting the 'day after' framing. Entry's cautionary note about no notice actually being filed in 2025 is accurate.

entries.title: Commission: only 24 of 6,018 Aland deletion requests were genuine
entries.summary: The Commission said Form 7 can be filed online but deletion requires notice and a hearing. In Aland, 6,018 deletion applications were filed online, only 24 were found genuine and accepted, and the ERO filed an FIR. In Rajura, 6,861 of 7,792 new-registration applications were rejected as invalid and an FIR was filed.
entries.attributed_to: Election Commission of India

sources.title: No deletion of any vote can be done online by any member of the public: ECI

entries.notes: Reported by AIR on 20 Sep 2025 (9:52 am) as a reiteration; the exact day the Commission released these figures was not verified.

entries.title: Commission calls Aland charge incorrect, says it filed the FIR itself
entries.summary: Within hours, the Commission posted that the allegations were incorrect and baseless, that no member of the public can delete a vote online, and that after unsuccessful deletion attempts in Aland in 2023 an FIR was filed by the Commission's own authority.
entries.attributed_to: Election Commission of India

sources.title: Election Commission rejects Rahul Gandhi's allegations on vote deletion as baseless
CEC shielding 'vote chors', undermining democracy: Rahul Gandhi; election panel rubbishes claim

entries.title: Rahul Gandhi alleges software-driven deletions in Aland, additions in Rajura
entries.summary: Rahul Gandhi alleged that 6,018 deletion applications in Aland, Karnataka, before the 2023 election were filed centrally using other voters' names and phone numbers, and that 6,850 names were added the same way in Rajura, Maharashtra. He said the Karnataka CID had written 18 letters in 18 months seeking IP, device and OTP data that the Commission did not provide, accused the CEC of protecting those responsible, and gave him a week to share the data.
entries.attributed_to: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, Lok Sabha

figures.label: Form 7 deletion applications in Aland cited by Rahul Gandhi

sources.title: Rahul Gandhi Presents Fresh Evidence On Electoral 'Fraud'
CEC shielding 'vote chors', undermining democracy: Rahul Gandhi; election panel rubbishes claim

entries.notes: The inc.in page is the party's own account (primary for the claim, not for its truth). The sources opened do not record a Commission answer on the 18 CID letters specifically.

entries.title: BJP's Ravi Shankar Prasad says Rahul Gandhi distorts facts on Commission
entries.summary: In Patna, senior BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad said Rahul Gandhi spoke without facts and noted that Gyanesh Kumar did not head the Commission at the time of the 2023 Karnataka election that the Aland charge concerns.
entries.attributed_to: Ravi Shankar Prasad, BJP

sources.title: BJP's Prasad: Rahul Gandhi Distorting Facts About Election Commission

entries.notes: No direct response to this statement was found in the sources opened.

verification.note: AIR's transcript confirms Prasad said Gandhi 'speaks without facts' and pointed out Kumar was not CEC during the 2023 Karnataka polls the Aland charge concerns, matching the entry.

entries.title: Reporters' Collective: Commission shared voter data with Telangana government
entries.summary: The Reporters' Collective reported that the Commission shared voter data including photographs with the Telangana government, which used private firms for a 2019 pensioner verification system, contrasting this with the CEC's stated reason for not releasing polling footage: voters' privacy.

sources.title: Election Commission gave access to voter data, including photos, to a state government and private companies
Telangana Election Official Confirms: Voter Data was Illegally Used by State Government

entries.notes: The Commission had not responded to written queries by publication, per the outlet. A further search for any later ECI response or rebuttal to this story found none.

verification.note: Both TRC pieces support the summary closely, including the contrast with CEC Kumar's privacy rationale for withholding polling footage and the Commission's non-response to written queries. No later ECI response to this story was found in a further search; the entry's notes already flag the non-response.

entries.title: Karnataka government sets up SIT on Aland deletion attempts
entries.summary: The Congress-led Karnataka government formed a Special Investigation Team under the CID's Additional Director General to probe the Aland deletion attempts, after a complaint by Aland MLA B R Patil.

sources.title: Karnataka Govt forms SIT to probe vote deletion allegations in Aland Assembly constituency

entries.title: Reporters' Collective: deduplication software not used in Bihar SIR
entries.summary: The Reporters' Collective reported, citing a senior Commission official and four EROs, that the Commission did not run its duplicate-detection software on the Bihar SIR roll, and that its analysis found 14.35 lakh suspect duplicate entries in the final Bihar roll.

figures.label: suspect duplicate entries in final Bihar roll (TRC analysis)

sources.title: ECI Skipped its Fraud-Busting Software, Flooding Bihar Voter Roll with Lakhs of Suspect Duplicates

entries.notes: Bihar's CEO had earlier said the draft roll's errors would be fixed before finalisation; the outlet says its questionnaire drew a meeting with the CEO. The Commission's court answer is recorded as its own entry.

entries.title: On Sandhu's direction, deputy tells IT chief statutory roll powers stay with EROs
entries.summary: Acting on Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu's directions, Deputy Election Commissioner Sanjay Kumar wrote to DG (IT) Seema Khanna and senior officers that the statutory functions of EROs, DEOs and CEOs must be exercised only by them and that IT systems must strictly comply with the law.

sources.title: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary's door over voter software integrity

entries.notes: The notes and letters are not public. This entry rests on The Indian Express's account of documents it says it has seen. The Commission and both Election Commissioners did not answer its questions (sent 21 Sep 2026).

verification.note: Article quotes the Nov 4, 2025 note verbatim: 'statutory functions of ERO, DEO and CEO (were) to be strictly exercised by them and no one else' and 'IT systems must be in strict compliance with the law' -- matches the entry exactly, including that Sanjay Kumar acted on Sandhu's direction.

entries.title: Commission sources: no appeals were filed against Haryana rolls
entries.summary: Unnamed Commission sources said there were zero appeals against Haryana's rolls and 22 election petitions pending, asked why Congress polling agents and booth agents did not object, and asked whether Rahul Gandhi supports the SIR, which removes duplicates.
entries.attributed_to: Election Commission of India (unnamed sources)

sources.title: 'Zero appeals against...': EC rebuts Rahul Gandhi's 'H Files' Haryana voter fraud allegations

entries.notes: Source-based, not an on-record Commission statement. The Haryana CEO's own post was not opened.

entries.title: Rahul Gandhi's 'H Files' allege 25 lakh fake entries in Haryana
entries.summary: Rahul Gandhi alleged that about 25 lakh entries in Haryana's roll for the 2024 Assembly election were fraudulent, including 5.21 lakh duplicates and 19.26 lakh bulk voters, and that one photo of a Brazilian model appeared 22 times under different names. He said the Commission was not removing duplicates to help the BJP.
entries.attributed_to: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, Lok Sabha

sources.title: 'Hydrogen Bomb' Unleashed: Rahul Gandhi Alleges 'Sarkar Chori' In Haryana, Claims One In Eight Voters 'Fake'

entries.title: Commission tells Supreme Court its duplicate-detection software was unreliable
entries.summary: In a counter-affidavit in the Supreme Court, responding to the Reporters' Collective finding cited in court, the Commission said the software's results were variable, many flagged entries were not duplicates, and the technology was last used in 2023.
entries.attributed_to: Election Commission of India (counter-affidavit, Supreme Court)

sources.title: ECI to Supreme Court: Deduplication Software Was Ineffective, We Scrapped It
sources.quote: The said technology was last used in 2023.

entries.notes: The affidavit itself was not opened; quoted as reproduced by the outlet. The outlet notes the Commission's 2023 roll manual ordered the software's use in 'campaign mode'.

entries.title: Lok Sabha debates electoral reforms; Rahul Gandhi presses on rolls and CCTV
entries.summary: In the Lok Sabha debate on electoral reforms, Rahul Gandhi alleged 1.2 lakh duplicate photos in the Bihar SIR roll, sought machine-readable rolls for parties a month before polls and withdrawal of the rule allowing CCTV footage to be destroyed. Congress's Manish Tewari questioned the SIR's legal basis. Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said SIRs were held several times under Congress governments.
entries.attributed_to: Rahul Gandhi (Congress), with Manish Tewari; government reply by Arjun Ram Meghwal, Law Minister

sources.title: Discussion Underway in Lok Sabha on Election Reforms

entries.notes: The Lok Sabha debate transcript on sansad.in was not opened.

entries.title: Amit Shah: SIR is the Commission's exclusive domain, not Parliament's
entries.summary: Replying to the debate, Home Minister Amit Shah said the SIR falls within the Commission's constitutional powers and cannot be answered by the government in Parliament, cited earlier intensive revisions under Congress governments, and said the exercise removes the dead, the shifted, duplicates and foreigners. When Rahul Gandhi asked him to debate his three press conferences, Shah said Parliament would not run to his wishes.
entries.attributed_to: Amit Shah, Union Home Minister

sources.title: SIR debate: Amit Shah, Rahul Gandhi face off in Lok Sabha
Rahul Gandhi challenges Shah to debate on his 3 PCs on 'vote chori'; Shah retorts

entries.title: Rahul Gandhi says Shah did not answer his vote-theft points
entries.summary: After an opposition walkout, Rahul Gandhi said the Home Minister's reply was defensive and did not address transparent rolls, EVMs or the immunity given to the CEC, and called vote theft the biggest treason.
entries.attributed_to: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, Lok Sabha

sources.title: Appeared under pressure: Rahul Gandhi takes dig at Amit Shah over Lok Sabha speech

entries.notes: No direct response to this statement was found in the sources opened.

entries.title: Deputy asks IT chief not to restrict ERO discretion in new SIR module
entries.summary: With the SIR under way in 12 states and UTs, Deputy Election Commissioner Sanjay Kumar asked DG (IT) Seema Khanna to ensure the IT system did not restrict EROs' discretion as the division moved them onto a new notice-and-hearing module.

sources.title: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary's door over voter software integrity

entries.notes: The notes and letters are not public. This entry rests on The Indian Express's account of documents it says it has seen. The Commission and both Election Commissioners did not answer its questions (sent 21 Sep 2026).

verification.note: Confirmed: on Jan 2, 2026, with SIR under way in 12 states/UTs, Sanjay Kumar asked Khanna to 'ensure that IT system is made in a manner that ERO's discretion to act in any manner is not restricted', exactly as summarised.

entries.title: CEC and IT chief say ECINet is lawful and builds public trust
entries.summary: At the launch of ECINet, which brought more than 40 Commission apps and portals together, CEC Gyanesh Kumar said it was built in strict accordance with the law and DG (IT) Seema Khanna said it would enhance transparency, credibility and public trust.

sources.title: Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary's door over voter software integrity

entries.notes: Launch statements as quoted by The Indian Express; the Commission's launch press note was not opened.

verification.note: Confirmed verbatim: CEC Kumar said ECINet was built 'in strict accordance with the law' and DG(IT) Khanna said it would 'enhance transparency, credibility and public trust' at the Jan 22, 2026 launch.

entries.title: Reporters' Collective: Commission's court account of notices contradicted
entries.summary: The Reporters' Collective reported that over 1.5 crore West Bengal SIR notices were generated by centralised, untested algorithms and signed off by overloaded EROs, contrary to the Commission's statement to the Supreme Court that there was no automated generation of notices.

sources.title: ECI misled the Supreme Court on SIR in West Bengal

entries.notes: The Commission had not responded to questions by publication, per the outlet. The Commission's court position was that EROs applied their minds to each notice.

entries.title: Reporters' Collective: Bengal SIR run through unpublished orders and WhatsApp
entries.summary: The Reporters' Collective reported that the Commission changed SIR rules in West Bengal without public notice, issued instructions over WhatsApp and orally, and placed roll observers whose approval EROs needed, turning statutory officers into intermediaries.

sources.title: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal 'As it Deemed Fit'
Verified: ECI's top West Bengal officer sent orders to state officials for SIR on WhatsApp

entries.notes: The Commission did not answer detailed questions by publication, per the outlet. It told the Supreme Court observers only assisted EROs, a position the court accepted on 9 Feb 2026 (per Scroll, 24 Sep 2026).

entries.title: Goa CEO writes eight times in seven days seeking rollback for 97 voters
entries.summary: Between 11 and 17 February, the Goa Chief Electoral Officer's office wrote eight times to Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Gyanesh Bharti, copying DG (IT) Seema Khanna, asking for a software rollback so EROs could reverse deletions of 97 electors they had found eligible under the Supreme Court's 29 January procedure. No reply is on record.

figures.label: electors found eligible by Goa EROs but left off final roll
electors who came forward after logical-discrepancy lists

sources.title: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out: EC's flawed system

entries.notes: The notes and letters are not public. This entry rests on The Indian Express's account of documents it says it has seen. The Commission and both Election Commissioners did not answer its questions (sent 21 Sep 2026). Seema Khanna did not answer a separate questionnaire on why the rollback was not enabled.

verification.note: Article gives the full email log (Feb 11, 13, 14x2+letter, 15, 16, 17) confirming 'his eighth time in seven days', addressed to Gyanesh Bharti with Khanna copied, and the exact figures of 97 eligible electors and 649 who came forward. Entry is accurate down to the figures.

entries.title: Deputy Election Commissioner: IT system cannot block Supreme Court-directed action
entries.summary: Deputy Election Commissioner Sanjay Kumar wrote to DG (IT) Seema Khanna that EROs had powers to correct the roll and the IT system could not block action required by the Supreme Court, asking her to enable the Goa EROs' decisions.

sources.title: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out: EC's flawed system

entries.notes: The notes and letters are not public. This entry rests on The Indian Express's account of documents it says it has seen. The Commission and both Election Commissioners did not answer its questions (sent 21 Sep 2026). The final Goa roll was published on 21 February without the 97; all 97 were still missing when the paper checked up to 20 Sep 2026.

verification.note: Confirmed verbatim: Feb 18 note from Sanjay Kumar to Khanna states EROs/AEROs have powers under s.21/21A and 'IT system cannot block necessary action as per the directions of SC', asking her to facilitate publication -- matches the entry precisely.

entries.title: Opposition files first-ever notices to remove a CEC in both Houses
entries.summary: Led by the TMC, opposition MPs submitted notices of motion to remove Gyanesh Kumar: 130 signatures in the Lok Sabha and 63 in the Rajya Sabha, above the 100 and 50 needed. The notices cited the SIR and alleged partisan and discriminatory conduct and obstruction of investigation into electoral fraud.
entries.attributed_to: Opposition MPs (TMC-led)

sources.title: Rajya Sabha Chairman, Lok Sabha Speaker reject Opposition move to impeach CEC Gyanesh Kumar

entries.notes: The notice texts were not opened.

verification.note: Confirmed: TMC-led notices filed March 12 with 130 LS and 63 RS signatures (above the 100/50 threshold), citing 'partisan and discriminatory conduct' and 'obstruction of investigation into electoral fraud and SIR' -- matches the entry.

entries.title: Speaker and Chairman refuse to admit CEC removal notices, no reasons given
entries.summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan refused to admit the notices under Section 3 of the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, through parliamentary bulletins that gave no reasons. TMC's Derek O'Brien and Congress's Jairam Ramesh criticised the decision.

sources.title: Rajya Sabha Chairman, Lok Sabha Speaker reject Opposition move to impeach CEC Gyanesh Kumar

entries.notes: The bulletins themselves were not opened; wording is as quoted by The Indian Express.

verification.note: Confirmed: both notices refused under Section 3 of the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, with bulletins giving no substantive reason, and both O'Brien's and Ramesh's reactions are quoted as summarised.

entries.title: Sandhu: communications issued in ECI's name without Commission's approval
entries.summary: Sukhbir Singh Sandhu told senior officers that many communications went out in the Commission's name without its approval and that all must now have it under the 2023 Act. He also recorded that the IT division had built new modules and portals without informing him, and that he learned of them from the media.

sources.title: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps
Election Commissioners knocked on Cabinet Secretary's door over voter software integrity

entries.notes: The notes and letters are not public. This entry rests on The Indian Express's account of documents it says it has seen. The Commission and both Election Commissioners did not answer its questions (sent 21 Sep 2026).

entries.title: 73 Rajya Sabha MPs file fresh notice with nine charges against CEC
entries.summary: Congress's Jairam Ramesh announced a notice signed by 73 Rajya Sabha MPs seeking the CEC's removal for 'proven misbehaviour'. Its nine charges include uneven enforcement of the Model Code, disenfranchisement through the West Bengal SIR, a defective nationwide SIR framework and repeated adverse court observations.
entries.attributed_to: 73 opposition Rajya Sabha MPs (announced by Jairam Ramesh, Congress)

entries.title: Rahul Gandhi: CEC should resign and 'turn approver'
entries.summary: At a press conference, Rahul Gandhi called the Prime Minister, Home Minister and CEC traitors, displayed photos of alleged 'conspirators', said Modi and Shah would one day be investigated, praised Sandhu and Joshi, and said Kumar turning approver would be an act of nationalism.
entries.attributed_to: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition, Lok Sabha

sources.title: CEC Gyanesh Kumar should resign, turn approver, says Rahul Gandhi
CEC must quit; Modi, Shah will face probe over 'vote chori': Rahul Gandhi

entries.notes: No BJP or Commission response to this press conference specifically was found; the Commission's 23 Sep press note is its standing response.

verification.note: Confirmed via Scroll and a fuller Tribune report: photos of alleged 'conspirators' including Modi, Shah, Doval, Bhagwat, Adani and Kumar; Modi/Shah 'will be investigated'; Sandhu and Joshi praised as 'patriotic'; Kumar urged to 'turn approver', called 'an act of nationalism'.

entries.title: Scroll: Bengal's roll process was centralised before Joshi's warning
entries.summary: Scroll reported that by May 2026, when Joshi warned of centralisation, the West Bengal SIR had already been run with centrally generated notices and observer approvals, and that over 91 lakh names were deleted though about a third of those people attended hearings.

figures.label: names deleted from West Bengal rolls in SIR (Scroll)

sources.title: Before election commissioners flagged 'centralisation' of voter rolls, it was done in Bengal SIR

verification.note: Confirmed: centrally generated notices, observers given a veto over EROs' decisions, and 'over 91 lakh' Bengal deletions with about a third of those affected having attended hearings -- matches the entry and its figure.

entries.title: BJP's Gaurav Bhatia: majority decisions are lawful; Congress lacks standing
entries.summary: In an op-ed, BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia argued that Section 18 of the 2023 Act and the 1995 T N Seshan ruling make majority decisions binding, so internal dissent does not undermine the Commission, and cited the Navin Chawla and M S Gill episodes against the Congress.
entries.attributed_to: Gaurav Bhatia, BJP national spokesperson

sources.title: Dissent is not dysfunction, institutions need it

entries.notes: The investigation's charge is that decisions were taken without the majority's knowledge, not that the majority overruled the CEC; the op-ed does not address that point directly.

entries.title: Congress protests nationwide for CEC's resignation; Patnaik joins demand
entries.summary: Congress workers protested in Lucknow, Kolkata, Chandigarh, Dehradun, Jammu and Guwahati, where state chief Gaurav Gogoi was detained. Priyanka Gandhi called the BJP's attack a stale story, and BJD president Naveen Patnaik sought the CEC's resignation and a review of the SIR.
entries.attributed_to: Indian National Congress; Naveen Patnaik, BJD

sources.title: Today India news live updates, 25 September 2026

entries.notes: No direct response to this statement was found. The Commission's standing reply to the investigation is its 23 Sep 2026 press note (statements-reporting-eci-press-note-differing-views).

verification.note: Full live-blog text confirms protests in Lucknow, Dehradun, Chandigarh, Kolkata, Guwahati and Jammu, Gaurav Gogoi's detention in Guwahati, Priyanka Gandhi's 'stale and weak story' quote, and Naveen Patnaik's resignation and SIR-review demand -- all match the entry precisely.

entries.title: Goa CEO: many of the 97 now enrolled through Form 6
entries.summary: The Goa CEO's office said the 97 cases left off the February final roll were processed separately through booth-level officer visits for fresh Form 6 applications, that many had been enrolled and the rest were being processed, and that no eligible elector would be left behind.
entries.attributed_to: Office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Goa (Sanjay Goel)

sources.title: After Express report, Goa CEO says cases of 97 voters 'processed separately'

entries.notes: The office did not give a number enrolled. The Commission headquarters and DG (IT) have not answered why the rollback was not enabled.

gaps: Primary text of the Commission's 23 Sep 2026 press note (signed by Deputy Director P Pawan) was not located on eci.gov.in or PIB; the entry relies on quotations in The Indian Express, The Tribune and Scroll. Look in ECI press releases for 23 Sep 2026.

The Sandhu and Joshi notes, the 29 Jul 2026 letters to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan and any reply, and the agenda or minutes of the 9 Sep 2026 Commission meeting are not public. Neither Election Commissioner has commented. Candidates: RTI to ECI and Cabinet Secretariat; parliamentary questions.

Parliamentary bulletins of 6 Apr 2026 rejecting the CEC removal notices, and the texts of the 12 Mar and 24 Apr 2026 notices (nine charges), were not opened. Look on sansad.in (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha bulletins Part II).

The Commission's official posts on X (8 Aug 2025 'sign or apologise'; 18 Sep 2025 Aland rebuttal) and the Karnataka, Maharashtra and Haryana CEO letters to Rahul Gandhi were known only through press reports; archive the originals.
No official transcript of the CEC's 17 Aug 2025 press conference was found; attendance of the two Election Commissioners there is unverified. Check ECI YouTube and eci.gov.in press notes.
The Commission's 24 Dec 2024 reply to the Congress on Maharashtra and its 12 Jun 2025 letter to Rahul Gandhi were cited by reports but not opened.

Lok Sabha debate on electoral reforms, 9-10 Dec 2025, not opened in the official transcript (sansad.in / eparlib.nic.in); Rahul Gandhi's specific questions (CJI's removal from the selection panel, CCTV-retention rule, CEC immunity) should be checked against it.
Whether the Commission ever answered the Karnataka CID's reported 18 letters on the Aland deletions (IP, device and OTP data), and the status of the Karnataka SIT, is unsourced.
The Commission's answer to the Haryana 'H Files' exists only as unnamed-source briefings; no on-record statement or Haryana CEO post was opened.
Whether the SIR declaration was removed from online Form 6 after 23 Sep 2026, and who approved adding it, is not established.
No response from the Commission or the Supreme Court to the 28 Jun 2026 opposition letter to the CJI was found.

Not collected because the search budget ran out: The Hindu's and Scroll's own data investigations of 2025-26 rolls; Reporters' Collective pieces of 7-10 Jul 2025 (Bihar roll), 22 Jul 2025 (citizenship burden), 28 Dec 2025 (algorithms mid-SIR) and 23 Jul 2026 (gender disclosures), with any Commission replies; Rahul Gandhi's 18 Sep 2026 'party chori' remark on the TMC symbol freeze (Deccan Herald); and any statement by the Law Ministry or PMO on the Indian Express investigation.
Mamata Banerjee's duplicate-EPIC allegation is dated to February 2025 only by month; find the exact date and whether the three-month unique-EPIC promise of 7 Mar 2025 was met.
